simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to מַמְתַּק (H4477) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: מַמְתַּק (mamtaq) means something sweet (literally or figuratively) First listed occurrence: Neh 8 10.

definitions.full: H4477. mamthaqqim מַמְתַֿקִּים noun [masculine] plural sweetness = sweet things ; — of drinks מ ׳וּשְׁתוּ Neh 8:10 (|| אִכְלוּ מַשְׁמַנִּים ); of lover's kisses מ ׳חִכּוֺ Song 5:16 (|| מַחֲמַדִּים כֻלּוֺ ).
